findings.title: Cleanup loop ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
findings.body: The ticker driving `CleanUpService.Run` was changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`. This is unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks) and is not mentioned anywhere in the PR description. This change affects every job scheduled through `clean()` - temp file cleanup, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, old annotations, user invites, stale short URLs, and stale query history - making all of them run up to 10x more often. Since `clean()` still has a 9-minute timeout (`const timeout = 9 * time.Minute`), a slow run can overlap with or immediately follow the next tick, effectively causing near-continuous execution of these maintenance jobs. This risks substantially increased DB/file-system load and could ironically reintroduce lock contention similar to the deadlock this PR is trying to fix. This looks like an accidental leftover from local testing and should be reverted or explicitly justified and tested.

findings.title: Routine, successful batch cleanup progress logged at Error level with full ID list dumps
findings.body: In `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579), every successful batch iteration logs via `r.log.Error(...)` even though no error occurred (the `err` field logged is always nil at that point, since the function already returned early on error). These log calls also include the full `ids` slice, which can contain up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` entries (the added test exercises a batch size of 32767). Because this loop runs until no more rows match and may run every minute now (see the ticker change in cleanup.go), this will flood logs with large ID dumps at Error severity on every normal run, which both degrades logging performance/storage and can trigger false-positive error alerting in production monitoring that treats Error-level logs as incidents. These should be downgraded to Debug/Info and should avoid dumping entire ID slices.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite literal ID list
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with a configured batch size greater than the 999 parameter limit, the code builds the literal `IN (...)` clause by repeatedly doing `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop over `ids`. This recreates and copies the growing string on every iteration, giving O(n^2) time/memory behavior. The PR's own test uses a batch size of 32767, meaning this path is exercised with tens of thousands of iterations, which is unnecessarily expensive compared to using a `strings.Builder` or the `strconv.AppendInt`-into-byte-slice pattern already used elsewhere in this same file (e.g., `getAccessControlFilter`).
